description: A PMID is canonical ASCII digits, or it is not sent (bmlib#470, bmlib#472, bmlib#478 at f4b7c52). A caller's PMID reaches Europe PMC's EXT_ID query, NCBI's ID Converter and efetch, so it is read once at the entry: surrounding whitespace is stripped, and whitespace is exactly the code points in stripped_whitespace (what Python's str.strip() removes; the apps trim this set, not Foundation's or Kotlin's own); a blank is no PMID and is not refused; ASCII digits [0-9]+ that are not all zeros are the PMID without their leading zeros (Europe PMC finds nothing for the padded form); 'PMC' then ASCII digits is a PMC ID given as a PMID and is read as one (pmc_id), with pmid null; anything else (a prefix, a suffix, a space inside, a sign, a decimal point, non-ASCII digits, all zeros, lower-case pmc) is refused, which the apps log naming the value and then proceed as though no PMID were given. A PMC ID given as a PMID fills the PMC ID only when the caller gave none. Python alone also reads integers (its digits; 0 is no PMID; bool is refused). Read by tests/test_identifiers.py, Packages/BioMedLit PMIDCanonicalTests and Android PmidCanonicalTest. A case gives its name, the input as text, the pmid read (null for none), the pmc_id read, and whether it was refused; a 'note' says why a case is there, and is read by no suite.

cases.name: trailing_zero_width_space_is_refused
cases.note: U+200B is not whitespace to Python's str.strip(); Foundation's whitespace set strips it, so the apps trim only stripped_whitespace.

cases.name: surrounding_next_line_is_stripped
cases.note: U+0085 is whitespace to Python's str.strip() but not to Kotlin's trim().

cases.name: surrounding_unit_separator_is_stripped
cases.note: U+001C to U+001F are whitespace to Python's str.strip() but not to Foundation's whitespacesAndNewlines.

cases.name: pmc_zero_is_read_as_a_pmc_id
cases.note: Current behaviour, pinned rather than endorsed: 'PMC' then ASCII digits is read as a PMC ID, all zeros included; no PMC record has that ID, so the lookup finds nothing.
